FWA holders upset that none of the substantial protocol fees generated during Fake World Assets’ initial two-week launch period were directed to token buybacks and instead went to TokenWorks.
Just last week this was shilled as Christ’s second coming
Source

tweet.text:
These sections of the docs have not changed since a week before launch. 

Yes, TokenWorks makes money. I'm personally of the belief that if you build an innovative product you should be rewarded, just as traders do. The goal is move future incoming fees (starting tomorrow) from going to TokenWorks to the token and make a sustainable protocol. 

There is no percentage of retroactive fees that would satisfy everyone. If you were hoping a large portion fees would be used for this I’m sorry, but it was never stated or even hinted at. I also don’t think it would do anything other than temporarily increase the token price, only for people to sell into it. 

I'd rather use it to keep building the protocol and add new features just like we've been planning from the start.

That being said, I do hear the feedback and I know everyone is just speaking from a place of wanting to see the protocol succeed. and for the protocol to succeed, more of the future fees need to stay within the ecosystem.

tweet.text:
Today, we're introducing @Intelligence_ai.

In 6 months, as a team of 10, we scaled from $5M to $60M ARR and 5.5M users across 190+ countries.

We raised a $7.9M seed, led by @IndexVentures with participation from @conviction, @A_StarVC, and @combinator to build DesignArena, a universal interface for accessing and evaluating the world's AI capabilities.

Most evaluations try to simulate the real-world. We believe the real-world is the ultimate verifier.

People come to @DesignArena with a request. Models compete to fulfill the request, and users determine what works best for them. 

Their live user behavior evaluates the models, improves how work is routed, and helps people access the right intelligence.

We've helped the world's leading frontier labs break the news on their SOTA capabilities.

POAP, the NFT proof-of-attendance protocol, winds down after 5+ years
Source

tweet.text:
After 5+ years, we're winding down POAP.

Over the years, we:
* minted millions of collectibles across hundreds of communities. 
* did incredible collaborations with world-class organizations - Coinbase, Amex, WMG, Bayer, and a long tail of others, including countless in crypto. 
* ran one of the biggest activations at Devcon, minting 8000+ collectibles over the course of a week. 
* built an Airport Rally to let collectors get POAPs at airports around the world. 

POAP meant something to a lot of people. 

Unfortunately, crypto's funding cycles and distribution dynamics made it hard to build a sustainable company without cannibalizing the ethos that made POAP mean something. Building on a fragile and quickly evolving stack, in the middle of an incredible hype cycle, only added to the challenges.
